questions.problems: D (hypothalamus releases ACTH) is weak for an MCAT examinee; C (posterior pituitary) is the only real trap.
Nap cortisol fell slightly more than rest (-1.2 vs -0.8), so 'similar' is a judgment call that a pedantic student might question, though no other option competes.

questions.ambiguity: B: a student may link unequal store placement to segregated neighborhoods, but segregation describes the separation of groups, not unequal access to resources.
C: self-rated health as a subjective measure is a common textbook objection, though it does not undercut the neighborhood-causes-health claim as directly.
questions.problems: The passage never says outright that individual income was not measured; the student must infer it from the grouping by median household income.
The phrase 'keeps the city's food supply running efficiently as a whole' nearly names functionalism, so the item is a giveaway.

questions.ambiguity: B: her blaming traffic for her own lateness is self-serving, but the stem's 'contrast between her two explanations' (other vs self) points to actor-observer bias.
B: the teachers' low expectations could be read as a Pygmalion/self-fulfilling-prophecy effect, though the stem describes a change in self-concept, not performance.
A: some prep sources blur role strain and role conflict, but here the demands come from two different roles, which is role conflict.

overall: The set reads much like real MCAT Psych/Soc material: plausible experimental passages, internally consistent tables (the nap mean 78 and the Quartile 1 car split of 31% both reconcile exactly), and good data-reasoning items (P1-2, P1-3, P2-6) whose distractors are built from real numbers in the passage. The strongest items are P1-2 and P2-3, which test baseline confounds and ecological inference the way the AAMC does. The weakest are P2-5, where the stem's wording nearly names functionalism, and a few discrete items (S6, S7, S4) that are straight definition recall and easier than most real exam items. Difficulty skews EASY to MODERATE, with only one item that is clearly HARD. No factual errors found.
